# Purpose

One pass over every phenotype folder. For each one it reads the real seed record,
the DeepGANnel record and the diffusion (DDPM) record, computes the same metric
set on the two synthetic arms, and then pools the five paired comparisons.

Every arm is scored identically.

```{r packages}

if (length(missing)) {
  stop("Install first: install.packages(c(\"",
       paste(missing, collapse = "\", \""), "\"))")
}

set.seed(42)
```

# Configuration

```{r config}
CFG <- list(
  # Paths
  pheno_root = "./Phenotypes",   # holds Phenotype_A, Phenotype_B, ...
  batch_dir  = "./batch_out",    # holds Phenotype_A_DDPM.parquet, ...
  out_dir    = "./benchmark_out",

  raw_pattern = "raw",           # substring marking the seed csv (case-insensitive)
  gan_pattern = "gan",           # substring marking the DeepGANnel csv
  only        = NULL,            # e.g. c("Phenotype_A") to run a subset

  # Recording parameters
  sample_hz  = 1e4,              # fallback only; a Time column takes precedence
  filter_hz  = 1e3,

  # Sample rate for generated files:
  #   "seed"  every arm uses the raw record's rate (generated time columns ignored)
  #   "own"   an arm with a time column uses its own rate
  rate_policy  = "seed",

  # Must match training
  seq_len     = 128,
  slow_factor = 64,

  # Analysis settings
  n_windows_mmd = 400,           # O(n^2) in the kernel: keep modest
  n_perm        = 200,
  # Spectral segment length. "auto" is resolved per phenotype (see below); a
  # number is applied to every phenotype and must fit all of them.
  psd_seg       = "auto",
  psd_seg_min   = 256,           # stop below this segment length
  psd_n_seg_min = 20,            # target segments per arm; fewer is flagged
  equalise_noise = TRUE,         # same segment and sample count for every arm
  acf_lag_max   = 200,
  # Conductance level for the noise segments. "auto" picks, per phenotype,
  # closed or open, whichever every arm can support.
  noise_level   = "auto",        # "auto", "closed" or "open"
  ks_subsample  = 2e5,
  # Amplitude-distribution equivalence test
  amp_win       = 1024, # window length (samples). Too short: noisy per-window
                        # histogram. Too long: picks up drift.
  n_windows_amp = 400,  # windows drawn per side
  amp_alpha     = 0.05, # one-sided equivalence significance level (gives a 90% CI)
  equiv_boot    = 500,  # window-pair / dwell bootstrap draws for the floor/arm
                        # KS-distance distributions (amplitude windows and dwell times)
  param_equiv_boot = 300, # block-bootstrap replicates for the two-Gaussian
                        # parametric amplitude equivalence test (EM fit per
                        # replicate, so lower than equiv_boot)
  # Delta for baseline/amplitude: a multiple of the median per-event noise SD
  # (see noise_sd_delta_for_param). Does not shrink with record length.
  noise_sd_k    = 1,    # margin = this many noise SDs
  event_min_len = 30,   # minimum open/closed run length (samples) for a
                        # per-event SD
  trace_secs    = 0.3,

  # Generation block geometry, used only by the block-join (seam) test.
  # Must match the settings diffusion_app.py generated with.
  block_len      = 32768,       # generation block length, samples
  context_len    = 512,         # carried context at block joins, samples
  env_time_secs  = 5,           # seconds of each record drawn in the envelope
                                # time-course plot; envelope metrics use the
                                # whole record
  long_record_secs = 10,        # seconds of each record drawn in the block-join
                                # plot; the join test uses the whole record

  # Optional extras
  do_manifold    = TRUE,        # UMAP / t-SNE, needs uwot + Rtsne, slow
  n_windows_proj = 400,

  proj_win       = 512,

  # ClusterSignificance on the manifold projections (Bioconductor package;
  # chunk skipped if absent). n_perm_cluster permutations per phenotype per
  # projection method.
  do_cluster_test = TRUE,
  n_perm_cluster  = 100,

  cache = FALSE                   # reuse per-phenotype results if present
  #Careful with caching, it can cause real confusion!!
)

dir.create(CFG$out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(CFG$out_dir, "cache"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

pal <- c("Real" = "#1b1b1b", "Diffusion" = "#c0392b", "GAN" = "#8e44ad",
         "Real floor" = "#7f8c8d", "White noise" = "#bdc3c7")

theme_channel <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
          legend.position = "top",
          legend.title = element_blank(),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "lines"),
          axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"))
}

# Figures saved as LZW-compressed TIFF. The device is opened directly so the
# compression argument reaches it (ggsave can drop it). ragg if installed
# (better text on Windows), else grDevices::tiff.
save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300) {
  path <- file.path(CFG$out_dir, paste0(name, ".tiff"))

  if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) {
    ragg::agg_tiff(path, width = width, height = height, units = "in",
                   res = dpi, compression = "lzw", background = "white")
  } else {
    grDevices::tiff(path, width = width, height = height, units = "in",
                    res = dpi, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
  }
  on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)

  print(plot)
  invisible(plot)
}

# kable() scaled to page width in PDF (latex_options ignored in HTML).
# hold_position keeps the table next to its caption.
nice_kable <- function(x, caption = NULL, ...) {
  if (!is.null(caption) && knitr::is_latex_output())
    caption <- gsub("([_$&%#])", "\\\\\\1", caption)
  knitr::kable(x, caption = caption, ...) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("scale_down", "hold_position"))
}
```

# Reading records

The seed and GAN csv files were not written by this pipeline, so their headers
cannot be assumed. Named columns are used when they are recognisable; otherwise
the columns are inferred the same way `batch_run.py` infers them. The resolved
mapping is printed in the manifest below.

```{r fn-read}
normalise_names <- function(nms) gsub("[_-]", " ", trimws(tolower(nms)))

# 10%-of-range quantisation, as in batch_run.py stage_seed()
quantise <- function(x) {
  span <- diff(range(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  if (span > 0) round(x / (0.1 * span)) else rep(0, length(x))
}

# A channels column may hold no more than this many discrete levels (MAX_LEVELS
# in batch_run.py). Used both to infer the column and to check a named one.
MAX_LEVELS <- 10

is_time_col <- function(x) {
  d <- diff(x)
  length(d) > 1 && all(d > 0) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(d, rep(d[1], length(d)), tolerance = 1e-3))
}

infer_cols <- function(df) {
  # The column count decides whether a time column exists at all: three columns
  # means one of them is time, two means there is none. Which one it is still
  # has to be found, because the order varies.
  time_col <- NA_integer_
  if (ncol(df) >= 3) {
    hit <- which(vapply(df, is_time_col, logical(1)))
    if (!length(hit)) {
      stop(ncol(df), " columns but none of them increases in constant steps, ",
           "so the time column cannot be identified")
    }
    time_col <- hit[1]
  }
  rest <- setdiff(seq_along(df), if (is.na(time_col)) integer(0) else time_col)
  lev  <- lapply(rest, function(j) sort(unique(quantise(df[[j]]))))
  n    <- vapply(lev, length, integer(1))
  k    <- which.min(n)
  if (n[k] > MAX_LEVELS) {
    stop("no column with <= ", MAX_LEVELS, " discrete levels; level counts ",
         paste(n, collapse = ", "))
  }
  others <- setdiff(seq_along(rest), k)
  list(time   = time_col,
       chan   = rest[k],
       cur    = rest[others[which.max(n[others])]],
       levels = lev[[k]])
}

read_record <- function(path) {
  df <- if (grepl("\\.parquet$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    as.data.frame(arrow::read_parquet(path))
  } else {
    d <- suppressWarnings(as.data.frame(
      readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal")))
    # A file with no header gets its first data row promoted to names; spot that
    # by the names parsing as numbers, and re-read.
    if (all(!is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(names(d)))))) {
      d <- as.data.frame(readr::read_csv(path, col_names = FALSE,
                                         show_col_types = FALSE))
    }
    d
  }

  df <- df[, vapply(df, function(x) is.numeric(x) || is.logical(x) ||
                      !all(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x))))),
                    logical(1)), drop = FALSE]
  df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x))))
  df <- df[stats::complete.cases(df), , drop = FALSE]
  if (ncol(df) < 2 || nrow(df) < 100) stop("too few usable rows/columns")

  nn  <- normalise_names(names(df))
  idx <- function(target) { h <- which(nn %in% target); if (length(h)) h[1] else NA_integer_ }
  i_chan <- idx(c("channels", "channel", "ideal", "idealisation", "idealization"))
  i_cur  <- idx(c("noisy current", "current", "raw", "raw current", "i"))
  i_time <- idx(c("time", "t"))

  # A recognised channels/current pair is used as named; otherwise columns are
  # inferred. Column order is not assumed.
  if (!is.na(i_chan) && !is.na(i_cur) && i_chan != i_cur) {
    how  <- "named columns"
    chan <- as.integer(round(df[[i_chan]]))
  } else {
    inf <- infer_cols(df)
    i_chan <- inf$chan; i_cur <- inf$cur; i_time <- inf$time
    how  <- "inferred"
    chan <- match(quantise(df[[i_chan]]), inf$levels) - 1L
  }

  out <- tibble::tibble(channels = as.numeric(chan),
                        current  = as.numeric(df[[i_cur]]))
  out$time <- if (!is.na(i_time)) as.numeric(df[[i_time]]) else
    (seq_len(nrow(out)) - 1) / CFG$sample_hz
  out <- dplyr::filter(out, is.finite(channels), is.finite(current))

  attr(out, "map") <- sprintf(
    "%s: chan=col%d cur=col%d time=%s", how, i_chan, i_cur,
    if (is.na(i_time)) sprintf("none, assuming %g Hz", CFG$sample_hz)
    else paste0("col", i_time))
  dplyr::select(out, time, channels, current)
}

fs_of <- function(d, fallback = CFG$sample_hz) {
  if (nrow(d) < 3) return(fallback)
  dt <- stats::median(diff(d$time), na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(dt) || dt <= 0) fallback else 1 / dt
}

# First n rows of a record, keeping the "map" attribute (subsetting drops it).
crop_rows <- function(d, n) {
  m <- attr(d, "map")
  d <- d[seq_len(n), ]
  attr(d, "map") <- m
  d
}
```

# Metric functions

```{r fn-metrics}
make_windows <- function(x, win, n_max = Inf, stride = NULL) {
  n <- length(x)
  if (n < win) return(matrix(numeric(0), nrow = 0, ncol = win))
  if (is.null(stride)) stride <- max(1L, floor((n - win) / max(1L, min(n_max, n))))
  starts <- seq(1L, n - win + 1L, by = stride)
  if (length(starts) > n_max) starts <- sample(starts, n_max)
  t(vapply(starts, function(s) x[s:(s + win - 1L)], numeric(win)))
}

sq_dists <- function(A, B) {
  pmax(outer(rowSums(A^2), rowSums(B^2), "+") - 2 * tcrossprod(A, B), 0)
}

# Median heuristic: gamma = 1 / median pairwise squared distance. The fixed 1/L
# used during training underflows to zero on current in pA and pins the
# statistic to its finite-sample floor.
median_gamma <- function(X, Y, n_sub = 200) {
  A <- X[sample(nrow(X), min(n_sub, nrow(X))), , drop = FALSE]
  B <- Y[sample(nrow(Y), min(n_sub, nrow(Y))), , drop = FALSE]
  m <- stats::median(sq_dists(A, B))
  if (!is.finite(m) || m <= 0) 1 / ncol(X) else 1 / m
}

mmd_rbf <- function(X, Y, gamma = NULL, unbiased = TRUE) {
  m <- nrow(X); n <- nrow(Y)
  if (m < 2 || n < 2) return(NA_real_)
  if (is.null(gamma)) gamma <- median_gamma(X, Y)
  Kxx <- exp(-gamma * sq_dists(X, X))
  Kyy <- exp(-gamma * sq_dists(Y, Y))
  Kxy <- exp(-gamma * sq_dists(X, Y))
  if (unbiased) {
    (sum(Kxx) - sum(diag(Kxx))) / (m * (m - 1)) +
      (sum(Kyy) - sum(diag(Kyy))) / (n * (n - 1)) - 2 * mean(Kxy)
  } else {
    mean(Kxx) + mean(Kyy) - 2 * mean(Kxy)
  }
}

mmd_permutation_p <- function(X, Y, n_perm = CFG$n_perm, gamma = NULL) {
  if (is.null(gamma)) gamma <- median_gamma(X, Y)
  obs <- mmd_rbf(X, Y, gamma)
  Z <- rbind(X, Y); m <- nrow(X)
  null <- replicate(n_perm, {
    i <- sample(nrow(Z))
    mmd_rbf(Z[i[seq_len(m)], , drop = FALSE], Z[i[-seq_len(m)], , drop = FALSE], gamma)
  })
  s <- stats::sd(null)
  list(mmd = obs,
       p   = (1 + sum(null >= obs)) / (n_perm + 1),
       z   = if (is.finite(s) && s > 0) (obs - mean(null)) / s else NA_real_)
}

# Noise segments are taken at a single conductance level so no gating step falls
# inside a segment. Runs are kept separate: concatenating them puts a step at
# every join, which adds broadband power and lowers the ACF.
at_level <- function(d, level) {
  if (identical(level, "closed")) d$channels == 0 else d$channels >= max(d$channels)
}

level_runs <- function(d, level, min_len = 1L) {
  r <- rle(at_level(d, level))
  ends <- cumsum(r$lengths); starts <- ends - r$lengths + 1
  keep <- which(r$values & r$lengths >= min_len)
  lapply(keep, function(i) d$current[starts[i]:ends[i]])
}

longest_at <- function(d, level) {
  r <- rle(at_level(d, level))
  if (!any(r$values)) 0L else max(r$lengths[r$values])
}

# Lengths of the runs at one level, without materialising the runs themselves.
# Used to choose a segment length before any spectrum is computed.
run_lengths_at <- function(d, level) {
  r <- rle(at_level(d, level))
  r$lengths[r$values]
}

# Number of Welch segments from a set of run lengths at 50% overlap (as in
# welch_psd).
seg_count <- function(lens, nperseg) {
  lens <- lens[lens >= nperseg]
  if (!length(lens)) return(0L)
  as.integer(sum(1L + (lens - nperseg) %/% (nperseg %/% 2L)))
}

# Welch across a list of runs: every segment from every run long enough to hold
# one contributes to a single average periodogram.
#
# n_seg_max thins the segments to a fixed count, spaced evenly across the record.
# Welch variance falls as 1/n_seg, so both synthetic arms are held to the same
# count.
welch_psd <- function(runs, fs, nperseg, n_seg_max = Inf) {
  if (is.numeric(runs)) runs <- list(runs)
  runs <- runs[vapply(runs, length, integer(1)) >= nperseg]
  if (!length(runs)) stop("no run at the chosen level holds ", nperseg, " samples")

  step <- nperseg %/% 2
  idx <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(runs), function(i)
    cbind(run = i, start = seq(1L, length(runs[[i]]) - nperseg + 1L, by = step))))
  n_avail <- nrow(idx)

  if (is.finite(n_seg_max) && n_seg_max < n_avail) {
    k <- as.integer(n_seg_max)
    idx <- idx[1L + ((0:(k - 1L)) * n_avail) %/% k, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  w <- 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2 * pi * (seq_len(nperseg) - 1) / (nperseg - 1))  # Hann
  U <- sum(w^2)
  acc <- numeric(nperseg %/% 2 + 1)
  for (r in seq_len(nrow(idx))) {
    s   <- idx[r, "start"]
    seg <- runs[[idx[r, "run"]]][s:(s + nperseg - 1L)]
    seg <- seg - mean(seg)
    X   <- stats::fft(seg * w)[seq_len(nperseg %/% 2 + 1)]
    acc <- acc + (Mod(X)^2) / (fs * U)
  }
  nseg <- nrow(idx)
  psd <- acc / nseg
  psd[-c(1, length(psd))] <- 2 * psd[-c(1, length(psd))]
  tibble::tibble(freq = seq(0, fs / 2, length.out = length(psd)), psd = psd,
                 n_seg = nseg, n_seg_avail = n_avail) |>
    dplyr::filter(freq > 0)
}

# Length-weighted mean of the per-run ACFs. n_max is a common sample budget per
# arm, spent on the runs in order; the run that crosses it is trimmed.
acf_of <- function(runs, lag_max, fs, n_max = Inf) {
  if (is.numeric(runs)) runs <- list(runs)
  runs <- runs[vapply(runs, length, integer(1)) > lag_max]
  if (!length(runs)) stop("no run at the chosen level is longer than ", lag_max,
                          " samples")

  if (is.finite(n_max)) {
    lens  <- vapply(runs, length, integer(1))
    spent <- c(0L, cumsum(lens))[seq_along(lens)]
    take  <- pmin(lens, pmax(0L, as.integer(n_max) - spent))
    keep  <- take > lag_max
    if (any(keep)) runs <- Map(function(x, k) x[seq_len(k)], runs[keep], take[keep])
  }

  w <- vapply(runs, length, integer(1))
  A <- vapply(runs, function(x)
    stats::acf(x - mean(x), lag.max = lag_max, plot = FALSE,
               demean = TRUE)$acf[, 1, 1], numeric(lag_max + 1))
  tibble::tibble(lag_n  = seq_len(lag_max + 1),
                 lag_ms = 1000 * (seq_len(lag_max + 1) - 1) / fs,
                 acf    = as.numeric(A %*% w / sum(w)),
                 n_used = sum(w))
}

dwell_times <- function(ideal, fs) {
  r <- rle(as.integer(round(ideal)))
  tibble::tibble(level = r$values, n_sample = r$lengths,
                 dwell_ms = 1000 * r$lengths / fs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(state = ifelse(level == 0, "Closed", "Open"))
}

# Half-amplitude idealiser. Two Gaussians of common width, fitted by EM.
# Soft responsibilities, since hard assignment fails when one level holds ~1% of
# the record. Polarity says which of the two fitted levels is closed.
idealise_half_amplitude <- function(current, unit_pA = NULL, baseline = NULL,
                                    n_levels = 1, polarity = 1) {
  x <- current[is.finite(current)]

  if (is.null(baseline) || is.null(unit_pA)) {
    # Fit on a regular subsample of 1e5 points (a 1% level still gives ~1000).
    xf <- if (length(x) > 1e5) x[seq(1, length(x), length.out = 1e5)] else x

    # Start means at the 0.1/99.9 percentiles; starting weight from the split
    # at the midpoint.
    mu  <- stats::quantile(xf, c(0.001, 0.999), names = FALSE)
    sg  <- max(stats::mad(xf), .Machine$double.eps^0.5)
    w   <- min(max(mean(xf < mean(mu)), 1e-3), 1 - 1e-3)
    tol <- 1e-8 * sg
    
    for (i in 1:300) {
      d1 <- stats::dnorm(xf, mu[1], sg) * w
      d2 <- stats::dnorm(xf, mu[2], sg) * (1 - w)
      r  <- d2 / (d1 + d2)
      r[!is.finite(r)] <- 0.5
      s2 <- sum(r); s1 <- sum(1 - r)
      if (s1 < 1 || s2 < 1) break
      new_mu <- c(sum((1 - r) * xf) / s1, sum(r * xf) / s2)
      new_sg <- max(sqrt((sum((1 - r) * (xf - new_mu[1])^2) +
                          sum(r * (xf - new_mu[2])^2)) / length(xf)),
                    .Machine$double.eps^0.5)
      w <- s1 / length(xf)
      done <- max(abs(c(new_mu - mu, new_sg - sg))) < tol
      mu <- new_mu; sg <- new_sg
      if (done) break
    }

    mu   <- sort(mu)
    shut <- if (polarity >= 0) mu[1] else mu[2]
    open <- if (polarity >= 0) mu[2] else mu[1]
    minority <- min(w, 1 - w)

    if (!is.finite(open - shut) || abs(open - shut) < 3 * sg ||
        minority < 5e-4) {
        out <- rep(NA_integer_, length(current))
        attr(out, "why") <- sprintf(
          "sep %.3g, width %.3g, rarer level %.3g",
          abs(open - shut), sg, minority)
        return(out)
    }

    if (is.null(baseline)) baseline <- shut
    if (is.null(unit_pA))  unit_pA  <- open - shut
  }

  lvl <- (current - baseline) / unit_pA
  pmin(pmax(as.integer(round(lvl)), 0L), as.integer(n_levels))
}

idealise_label_anchored_cv <- function(
    current,
    labels,
    n_levels = 1L,
    polarity = 1,
    block_len = 1000L,
    trim = 0.10,
    min_state_n = 50L
) {
  stopifnot(length(current) == length(labels))

  ok <- is.finite(current) & is.finite(labels)
  labels <- as.integer(labels > 0)

  n <- length(current)
  block <- ((seq_len(n) - 1L) %/% block_len) + 1L
  fold <- block %% 2L

  recovered <- rep(NA_integer_, n)
  fit_info <- vector("list", 2L)

  robust_centre <- function(x) {
    x <- x[is.finite(x)]

    if (!length(x)) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    mean(x, trim = trim)
  }

  for (test_fold in 0:1) {
    train <- ok & fold != test_fold
    test  <- ok & fold == test_fold

    x_closed <- current[train & labels == 0L]
    x_open   <- current[train & labels > 0L]

    if (length(x_closed) < min_state_n ||
        length(x_open) < min_state_n) {
      next
    }

    closed_centre <- robust_centre(x_closed)
    open_centre   <- robust_centre(x_open)

    if (!is.finite(closed_centre) ||
        !is.finite(open_centre) ||
        closed_centre == open_centre) {
      next
    }

    # Respect the polarity defined from the real record.
    if (polarity >= 0) {
      baseline <- closed_centre
      unit_pA  <- open_centre - closed_centre
    } else {
      baseline <- closed_centre
      unit_pA  <- open_centre - closed_centre
    }

    lvl <- (current[test] - baseline) / unit_pA

    recovered[test] <- pmin(
      pmax(as.integer(round(lvl)), 0L),
      as.integer(n_levels)
    )

    fit_info[[test_fold + 1L]] <- list(
      n_closed = length(x_closed),
      n_open = length(x_open),
      baseline = baseline,
      open_centre = open_centre,
      unit_pA = unit_pA
    )
  }

  if (all(is.na(recovered))) {
    attr(recovered, "why") <-
      "cross-fitted label anchoring lacked enough observations in one or both states"
  }

  attr(recovered, "fit") <- fit_info
  attr(recovered, "method") <- "cross-fitted label-anchored half-amplitude"

  recovered
}
# Cohen's kappa on two logical vectors (corrects for the high chance agreement
# of records that are nearly always open or nearly always closed).
cohen_kappa <- function(a, b) {
  po <- mean(a == b)
  pe <- mean(a) * mean(b) + mean(!a) * mean(!b)
  if (!is.finite(pe) || pe >= 1) NA_real_ else (po - pe) / (1 - pe)
}

block_mean <- function(x, factor) {
  factor <- max(1L, as.integer(factor))
  nb <- length(x) %/% factor
  if (nb < 1) return(mean(x))
  colMeans(matrix(x[seq_len(nb * factor)], nrow = factor))
}

ks_safe <- function(a, b, n_max = CFG$ks_subsample) {
  a <- a[is.finite(a)]; b <- b[is.finite(b)]
  if (length(a) > n_max) a <- sample(a, n_max)
  if (length(b) > n_max) b <- sample(b, n_max)
  suppressWarnings(stats::ks.test(a, b))
}

# Amplitude equivalence: one-sided window-based test on KS distance
# Tests the whole amplitude distribution (spread and shape as well as location).
# Unit of comparison is a window of CFG$amp_win samples. Delta comes from real
# alone: KS D between random pairs of real windows, one from each half of the
# record. KS D is a non-negative distance, so the test is one-sided at
# CFG$amp_alpha (Wellek, 2010): Delta is the (1 - alpha) quantile of the
# real/real floor, and an arm is equivalent if the (1 - alpha) quantile of the
# real/arm distances is below Delta.
amplitude_floor_windows <- function(real_x, win = CFG$amp_win,
                                     n_windows = CFG$n_windows_amp,
                                     B = CFG$equiv_boot,
                                     alpha = CFG$amp_alpha) {
  n <- length(real_x); half <- n %/% 2L
  W1 <- make_windows(real_x[1:half],       win, n_windows)
  W2 <- make_windows(real_x[(half + 1):n], win, n_windows)
  floor_d <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(i) {
    a <- W1[sample.int(nrow(W1), 1), ]
    b <- W2[sample.int(nrow(W2), 1), ]
    ks_safe(a, b)$statistic
  }, numeric(1))
  unname(stats::quantile(floor_d, 1 - alpha))
}

amplitude_equiv_windows <- function(real_x, arm_x, delta,
                                     win = CFG$amp_win,
                                     n_windows = CFG$n_windows_amp,
                                     B = CFG$equiv_boot,
                                     alpha = CFG$amp_alpha) {
  Wr <- make_windows(real_x, win, n_windows)
  Wa <- make_windows(arm_x,  win, n_windows)
  arm_d <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(i) {
    a <- Wr[sample.int(nrow(Wr), 1), ]
    b <- Wa[sample.int(nrow(Wa), 1), ]
    ks_safe(a, b)$statistic
  }, numeric(1))
  upper <- unname(stats::quantile(arm_d, 1 - alpha))
  p <- (1 + sum(arm_d >= delta)) / (length(arm_d) + 1)  # H0: true D >= Delta

  list(upper = upper, p = p, equivalent = upper < delta)
}

# Parametric amplitude equivalence: two-Gaussian EM fit
# Two Gaussians of common width (closed and open levels) fitted to the amplitude
# histogram. Baseline, unitary amplitude, common SD and open weight (fit-based
# Popen) are signed parameters, tested by TOST with a 90% CI (Schuirmann, 1987).
# Same EM as idealise_half_amplitude(), returning the fitted parameters.
fit_two_gaussian_em <- function(x, polarity = 1) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  xf <- if (n > 1e5) x[seq(1, n, length.out = 1e5)] else x
  nf <- length(xf)

  mu  <- stats::quantile(xf, c(0.001, 0.999), names = FALSE)
  sg  <- max(stats::mad(xf), .Machine$double.eps^0.5)
  w   <- min(max(mean(xf < mean(mu)), 1e-3), 1 - 1e-3)
  tol <- 1e-8 * sg

  for (i in 1:300) {
    d1 <- stats::dnorm(xf, mu[1], sg) * w
    d2 <- stats::dnorm(xf, mu[2], sg) * (1 - w)
    r  <- d2 / (d1 + d2)
    r[!is.finite(r)] <- 0.5
    s2 <- sum(r); s1 <- sum(1 - r)
    if (s1 < 1 || s2 < 1) break
    new_mu <- c(sum((1 - r) * xf) / s1, sum(r * xf) / s2)
    new_sg <- max(sqrt((sum((1 - r) * (xf - new_mu[1])^2) +
                        sum(r * (xf - new_mu[2])^2)) / nf),
                  .Machine$double.eps^0.5)
    w <- s1 / nf
    done <- max(abs(c(new_mu - mu, new_sg - sg))) < tol
    mu <- new_mu; sg <- new_sg
    if (done) break
  }

  mu   <- sort(mu)
  shut <- if (polarity >= 0) mu[1] else mu[2]
  open <- if (polarity >= 0) mu[2] else mu[1]
  minority <- min(w, 1 - w)
  popen_w  <- if (polarity >= 0) 1 - w else w
  ok <- is.finite(open - shut) && abs(open - shut) >= 3 * sg && minority >= 5e-4

  list(baseline = unname(shut), amplitude = unname(open - shut),
       sd = sg, weight = popen_w, ok = ok)
}

# Parametric amplitude equivalence: single-Beta fallback
# For records whose real trace fails two-Gaussian separation (e.g. Phenotype_D,
# ~97% of its bootstrap replicates). One Beta component, which allows skewed
# noise. Reports only "location" and "spread" (fitted mean and SD, pA) under
# their own metric names. Mode is set once per phenotype from the full real
# trace (see "param_mode"), so real and both arms are fitted the same way.
# x is rescaled to (0, 1) with a fixed lo/hi from real's range (padded 1% each
# side), shared by real and both arms; values outside are clipped.
fit_beta_single <- function(x, lo, hi, eps = 1e-4) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  # Subsample to 1e5 points, as in fit_two_gaussian_em (runs inside a bootstrap
  # loop).
  n <- length(x)
  x <- if (n > 1e5) x[seq(1, n, length.out = 1e5)] else x
  span <- hi - lo
  u <- (x - lo) / span
  u <- pmin(pmax(u, eps), 1 - eps)

  m <- mean(u); v <- max(stats::var(u), 1e-8)
  k  <- m * (1 - m) / v - 1
  a0 <- max(m * k, 1e-2)
  b0 <- max((1 - m) * k, 1e-2)

  nll <- function(par) {
    a <- exp(par[1]); b <- exp(par[2])
    -sum(stats::dbeta(u, a, b, log = TRUE))
  }
  fit <- tryCatch(
    stats::optim(log(c(a0, b0)), nll, method = "Nelder-Mead",
                 control = list(maxit = 500)),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(fit) || fit$convergence != 0) {
    return(list(location = NA_real_, spread = NA_real_, ok = FALSE))
  }
  a <- exp(fit$par[1]); b <- exp(fit$par[2])
  mean_u <- a / (a + b)
  sd_u   <- sqrt(a * b / ((a + b)^2 * (a + b + 1)))
  list(location = lo + mean_u * span, spread = sd_u * span, ok = TRUE)
}

# Dispatch to the Gaussian or Beta fit by mode.
fit_amp_component <- function(x, polarity, mode = "gaussian", beta_range = NULL) {
  if (identical(mode, "beta")) return(fit_beta_single(x, beta_range[1], beta_range[2]))
  fit_two_gaussian_em(x, polarity)
}

# Block bootstrap: resample contiguous blocks with replacement to keep local
# autocorrelation. Used for the parametric fit, which needs full-length
# replicates (a single amp_win window rarely holds enough openings).
block_bootstrap_1d <- function(x, block_len, n_out) {
  n <- length(x)
  n_blocks <- ceiling(n_out / block_len)
  starts <- sample.int(n - block_len + 1L, n_blocks, replace = TRUE)
  out <- unlist(lapply(starts, function(s) x[s:(s + block_len - 1L)]))
  out[seq_len(n_out)]
}

dwell_block_len <- function(channels, mult = 10, lo = 50L, hi = 5000L) {
  runs <- rle(channels)$lengths
  as.integer(max(lo, min(hi, mult * mean(runs))))
}

# Three sets of real-only block-bootstrap fits, made once per phenotype and
# shared by both arms and all parameters: f1/f2 give Delta (the floor), fr is
# compared with each arm's bootstrap fits.
param_floor_fits <- function(real_x, real_channels, polarity, mode = "gaussian",
                              beta_range = NULL, B = CFG$param_equiv_boot) {
  bl <- dwell_block_len(real_channels)
  n  <- length(real_x)
  rep_fit <- function()
    fit_amp_component(block_bootstrap_1d(real_x, bl, n), polarity, mode, beta_range)
  list(f1 = replicate(B, rep_fit(), simplify = FALSE),
       f2 = replicate(B, rep_fit(), simplify = FALSE),
       fr = replicate(B, rep_fit(), simplify = FALSE))
}

param_arm_fits <- function(arm_x, real_channels, polarity, mode = "gaussian",
                            beta_range = NULL, B = CFG$param_equiv_boot) {
  # Block length from real's dwell structure, as for Delta.
  bl <- dwell_block_len(real_channels)
  replicate(B, fit_amp_component(block_bootstrap_1d(arm_x, bl, length(arm_x)), polarity,
                                  mode, beta_range),
            simplify = FALSE)
}

# Delta from real alone (f1 vs f2).
param_delta_field <- function(floor_fits, field) {
  ok1 <- vapply(floor_fits$f1, `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  ok2 <- vapply(floor_fits$f2, `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  keep <- ok1 & ok2
  n <- sum(keep)
  if (n < 20) return(list(ok = FALSE, n = n))
  val <- function(fits) vapply(fits, `[[`, numeric(1), field)
  floor_diff <- val(floor_fits$f1)[keep] - val(floor_fits$f2)[keep]
  list(ok = TRUE, n = n, delta = unname(stats::quantile(abs(floor_diff), 0.90)))
}

param_equiv_field <- function(floor_fits, arm_fits, field, delta) {
  ok_r <- vapply(floor_fits$fr, `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  ok_a <- vapply(arm_fits,      `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  keep <- ok_r & ok_a
  n_ok <- sum(keep)
  if (n_ok < 20) return(list(ok = FALSE, n_ok = n_ok))
  val <- function(fits) vapply(fits, `[[`, numeric(1), field)
  diff_boot <- val(floor_fits$fr)[keep] - val(arm_fits)[keep]
  ci <- unname(stats::quantile(diff_boot, c(0.05, 0.95)))
  p1 <- (1 + sum(diff_boot <= -delta)) / (n_ok + 1)  # H01: true diff <= -Delta
  p2 <- (1 + sum(diff_boot >=  delta)) / (n_ok + 1)  # H02: true diff >= +Delta
  list(ok = TRUE, n_ok = n_ok, ci_lo = ci[1], ci_hi = ci[2], p = max(p1, p2),
       equivalent = ci[1] > -delta && ci[2] < delta)
}

# Dwell-time distribution equivalence
# One-sided KS-distance test on the full open and closed dwell-time
# distributions, bootstrapping the dwell durations directly (Wellek, 2010).
dwell_delta <- function(real_dwell, B = CFG$equiv_boot, alpha = CFG$amp_alpha) {
  n <- length(real_dwell)
  if (n < 20) return(list(ok = FALSE, n = n))
  half <- n %/% 2L
  r1 <- real_dwell[1:half]; r2 <- real_dwell[(half + 1):n]
  floor_d <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(i) {
    a <- sample(r1, length(r1), replace = TRUE)
    b <- sample(r2, length(r2), replace = TRUE)
    ks_safe(a, b)$statistic
  }, numeric(1))
  list(ok = TRUE, n = n, delta = unname(stats::quantile(floor_d, 1 - alpha)))
}

dwell_equiv <- function(real_dwell, arm_dwell, delta,
                         B = CFG$equiv_boot, alpha = CFG$amp_alpha) {
  if (length(arm_dwell) < 20) return(list(ok = FALSE, n = length(arm_dwell)))
  arm_d <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(i) {
    a <- sample(real_dwell, length(real_dwell), replace = TRUE)
    b <- sample(arm_dwell,  length(arm_dwell),  replace = TRUE)
    ks_safe(a, b)$statistic
  }, numeric(1))
  upper <- unname(stats::quantile(arm_d, 1 - alpha))
  p <- (1 + sum(arm_d >= delta)) / (length(arm_d) + 1)
  list(ok = TRUE, upper = upper, p = p, equivalent = upper < delta,
       n_real = length(real_dwell), n_arm = length(arm_dwell))
}

# Noise SD by event
# One SD per open/closed run of at least CFG$event_min_len samples, using the
# same run detection as dwell_times.
noise_sd_by_event <- function(current, channels, state, min_len = CFG$event_min_len) {
  r <- rle(as.integer(round(channels)))
  ends   <- cumsum(r$lengths)
  starts <- ends - r$lengths + 1L
  run_state <- ifelse(r$values == 0, "Closed", "Open")
  keep <- run_state == state & r$lengths >= min_len
  if (!any(keep)) return(numeric(0))
  vapply(which(keep), function(i) stats::sd(current[starts[i]:ends[i]]), numeric(1))
}

# Noise-SD Delta for the parametric baseline/amplitude TOST
# Delta = CFG$noise_sd_k x the real record's pooled per-event noise SD (closed
# events for baseline, open events for amplitude). A bootstrap Delta shrinks as
# the record gets longer; the noise SD converges to a fixed value. Gaussian mode
# only; Beta mode keeps the bootstrap Delta from param_delta_field.
# Pooled SD weights each event by its degrees of freedom (n - 1).
pooled_event_sd <- function(current, channels, state, min_len = CFG$event_min_len) {
  r <- rle(as.integer(round(channels)))
  ends   <- cumsum(r$lengths)
  starts <- ends - r$lengths + 1L
  run_state <- ifelse(r$values == 0, "Closed", "Open")
  keep <- run_state == state & r$lengths >= min_len
  if (!any(keep)) return(list(ok = FALSE, n = 0L))
  idx <- which(keep)
  sds <- vapply(idx, function(i) stats::sd(current[starts[i]:ends[i]]), numeric(1))
  ns  <- r$lengths[idx]
  pooled_var <- sum((ns - 1) * sds^2) / sum(ns - 1)
  list(ok = TRUE, n = length(idx), sd = sqrt(pooled_var))
}

noise_sd_delta_for_param <- function(field, real_x, real_channels,
                                      k = CFG$noise_sd_k) {
  state  <- if (identical(field, "baseline")) "Closed" else "Open"
  pooled <- pooled_event_sd(real_x, real_channels, state)
  if (!pooled$ok || pooled$n < 3) return(list(ok = FALSE, n = pooled$n))
  list(ok = TRUE, n = pooled$n, delta = k * pooled$sd)
}

# Baseline/amplitude from the channels column
# A second estimate alongside the two-Gaussian/Beta fit (which does not use the
# labels): baseline = median(current) where channels == 0, amplitude =
# median(current) where channels > 0, minus baseline, as in the preflight
# inventory. Needs only some closed- and some open-labelled samples.
channels_baseline_amplitude <- function(current, channels) {
  closed <- current[channels == 0]
  open   <- current[channels > 0]
  if (!length(closed) || !length(open)) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, n_closed = length(closed), n_open = length(open)))
  }
  baseline <- stats::median(closed)
  list(ok = TRUE, n_closed = length(closed), n_open = length(open),
       baseline = baseline, amplitude = stats::median(open) - baseline)
}

# Block bootstrap of current and channels together, keeping each sample paired
# with its state.
paired_block_bootstrap <- function(current, channels, block_len, n_out) {
  n <- length(current)
  n_blocks <- ceiling(n_out / block_len)
  starts <- sample.int(n - block_len + 1L, n_blocks, replace = TRUE)
  idx <- unlist(lapply(starts, function(s) s:(s + block_len - 1L)))[seq_len(n_out)]
  list(current = current[idx], channels = channels[idx])
}

# Real-only block-bootstrap replicates of (current, channels), shared by both
# arms. One set only: Delta comes from noise_sd_delta_for_param.
channels_amp_real_reps <- function(real_x, real_channels, B = CFG$param_equiv_boot) {
  bl <- dwell_block_len(real_channels)
  n  <- length(real_x)
  replicate(B, {
    r <- paired_block_bootstrap(real_x, real_channels, bl, n)
    channels_baseline_amplitude(r$current, r$channels)
  }, simplify = FALSE)
}

channels_amp_arm_reps <- function(arm_x, arm_channels, real_channels,
                                   B = CFG$param_equiv_boot) {
  # Block length from real's dwell structure.
  bl <- dwell_block_len(real_channels)
  n  <- length(arm_x)
  replicate(B, {
    r <- paired_block_bootstrap(arm_x, arm_channels, bl, n)
    channels_baseline_amplitude(r$current, r$channels)
  }, simplify = FALSE)
}

# TOST (90% CI) on the real-vs-arm bootstrap difference of the channels-based
# estimate.
channels_amp_equiv <- function(real_reps, arm_reps, field, delta) {
  ok_r <- vapply(real_reps, `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  ok_a <- vapply(arm_reps,  `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  keep <- ok_r & ok_a
  n_ok <- sum(keep)
  if (n_ok < 20) return(list(ok = FALSE, n_ok = n_ok))
  val <- function(reps) vapply(reps, `[[`, numeric(1), field)
  diff_boot <- val(real_reps)[keep] - val(arm_reps)[keep]
  ci <- unname(stats::quantile(diff_boot, c(0.05, 0.95)))
  p1 <- (1 + sum(diff_boot <= -delta)) / (n_ok + 1)
  p2 <- (1 + sum(diff_boot >=  delta)) / (n_ok + 1)
  list(ok = TRUE, n_ok = n_ok, ci_lo = ci[1], ci_hi = ci[2], p = max(p1, p2),
       equivalent = ci[1] > -delta && ci[2] < delta)
}

# Baseline/amplitude, relative margin
# Difference as a fraction of unitary amplitude. The amplitude is recomputed on
# each bootstrap replicate, so its sampling uncertainty enters the CI.
# Delta_rel(field) = k x (real's pooled per-event noise SD for that state) /
# (real's point-estimate amplitude), from real alone.
channels_amp_relative_delta <- function(field, real_x, real_channels,
                                         real_amplitude_pt, k = CFG$noise_sd_k) {
  state  <- if (identical(field, "baseline")) "Closed" else "Open"
  pooled <- pooled_event_sd(real_x, real_channels, state)
  if (!pooled$ok || pooled$n < 3) return(list(ok = FALSE, n = pooled$n))
  if (!is.finite(real_amplitude_pt) || real_amplitude_pt == 0) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, n = pooled$n))
  }
  list(ok = TRUE, n = pooled$n, delta = k * pooled$sd / abs(real_amplitude_pt))
}

# Uses the replicates from channels_amp_equiv. Relative difference per draw =
# (real field - arm field) / that draw's real amplitude. Draws whose amplitude
# is below guard_frac x the point estimate are discarded and counted.
channels_amp_relative_equiv <- function(real_reps, arm_reps, field, delta,
                                         real_amplitude_pt, guard_frac = 0.1) {
  ok_r  <- vapply(real_reps, `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  ok_a  <- vapply(arm_reps,  `[[`, logical(1), "ok")
  amp_r <- vapply(real_reps, function(r) if (r$ok) r$amplitude else NA_real_, numeric(1))
  guard <- guard_frac * abs(real_amplitude_pt)
  fit_ok <- ok_r & ok_a
  keep   <- fit_ok & is.finite(amp_r) & abs(amp_r) >= guard
  n_ok <- sum(keep)
  n_discarded_fitfail <- sum(!fit_ok)
  n_discarded_guard    <- sum(fit_ok & (!is.finite(amp_r) | abs(amp_r) < guard))
  if (n_ok < 20) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, n_ok = n_ok, n_discarded_guard = n_discarded_guard,
                n_discarded_fitfail = n_discarded_fitfail))
  }
  val <- function(reps, f) vapply(reps, `[[`, numeric(1), f)
  rel_diff <- (val(real_reps, field)[keep] - val(arm_reps, field)[keep]) / amp_r[keep]
  ci <- unname(stats::quantile(rel_diff, c(0.05, 0.95)))
  p1 <- (1 + sum(rel_diff <= -delta)) / (n_ok + 1)
  p2 <- (1 + sum(rel_diff >=  delta)) / (n_ok + 1)
  list(ok = TRUE, n_ok = n_ok, n_discarded_guard = n_discarded_guard,
       n_discarded_fitfail = n_discarded_fitfail,
       ci_lo = ci[1], ci_hi = ci[2], p = max(p1, p2),
       equivalent = ci[1] > -delta && ci[2] < delta)
}

# Noise-SD distribution equivalence and Popen equivalence
# One-sided KS-distance tests (Wellek, 2010) on distributions.
# Noise SD: per-event SDs, through dwell_delta/dwell_equiv.
# Popen: one value per window of CFG$amp_win samples, then an ordinary
# bootstrap over the per-window values.
window_popen <- function(channels, win = CFG$amp_win, n_windows = CFG$n_windows_amp) {
  W <- make_windows(channels, win, n_windows)
  if (nrow(W) == 0) return(numeric(0))
  rowMeans(W > 0)
}

popen_delta <- function(real_channels, win = CFG$amp_win, n_windows = CFG$n_windows_amp,
                         B = CFG$equiv_boot, alpha = CFG$amp_alpha) {
  n <- length(real_channels); half <- n %/% 2L
  # Windows from each half of real, so the two vectors share no window.
  p1 <- window_popen(real_channels[1:half],       win, n_windows)
  p2 <- window_popen(real_channels[(half + 1):n], win, n_windows)
  if (length(p1) < 20 || length(p2) < 20) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, n = min(length(p1), length(p2))))
  }
  floor_d <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(i) {
    a <- sample(p1, length(p1), replace = TRUE)
    b <- sample(p2, length(p2), replace = TRUE)
    ks_safe(a, b)$statistic
  }, numeric(1))
  list(ok = TRUE, n = length(p1) + length(p2),
       delta = unname(stats::quantile(floor_d, 1 - alpha)))
}

popen_equiv <- function(real_channels, arm_channels, delta,
                         win = CFG$amp_win, n_windows = CFG$n_windows_amp,
                         B = CFG$equiv_boot, alpha = CFG$amp_alpha) {
  pr <- window_popen(real_channels, win, n_windows)
  pa <- window_popen(arm_channels,  win, n_windows)
  if (length(pr) < 20 || length(pa) < 20) return(list(ok = FALSE, n = length(pa)))
  arm_d <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(i) {
    a <- sample(pr, length(pr), replace = TRUE)
    b <- sample(pa, length(pa), replace = TRUE)
    ks_safe(a, b)$statistic
  }, numeric(1))
  upper <- unname(stats::quantile(arm_d, 1 - alpha))
  p <- (1 + sum(arm_d >= delta)) / (length(arm_d) + 1)
  list(ok = TRUE, upper = upper, p = p, equivalent = upper < delta,
       n_real = length(pr), n_arm = length(pa))
}

# Window for the example traces, as _best_window in batch_run.py: a stretch
# with Popen in [lo, hi], else the one nearest the middle of that band.
best_window <- function(chan, n, lo = 0.4, hi = 0.8) {
  if (length(chan) <= n) return(1L)
  cs <- c(0, cumsum(as.numeric(chan)))
  k  <- (cs[(n + 1):length(cs)] - cs[1:(length(cs) - n)]) / n
  inside <- which(k >= lo & k <= hi)
  if (length(inside)) return(inside[ceiling(length(inside) / 2)])
  which.min(abs(k - 0.5 * (lo + hi)))
}

rms_diff <- function(a, b) sqrt(mean((a - b)^2))

# Two-component exponential mixture fitted to dwell times by EM. Falls back to
# one component if the slow/fast ratio is under min_ratio or a component holds
# almost no area (as in fit_tcrit). Dwells only a few samples long (e.g. 0.39 ms
# at 10 kHz) also give one component.
fit_exp_mixture <- function(x, n_iter = 500, tol = 1e-10, min_n = 20L,
                            min_ratio = 3, min_area = 0.02) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]

  one <- function() tibble::tibble(
    n_components = 1L,
    tau_fast_ms  = if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_,
    tau_slow_ms  = NA_real_,
    area_fast    = NA_real_,
    mean_ms      = if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_,
    n_events     = length(x))

  if (length(x) < min_n) return(one())

  tau <- as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.9), names = FALSE))
  if (!(tau[2] > tau[1])) return(one())
  a <- c(0.5, 0.5)
  ll_old <- -Inf

  for (i in seq_len(n_iter)) {
    d <- cbind(a[1] * stats::dexp(x, 1 / tau[1]),
               a[2] * stats::dexp(x, 1 / tau[2]))
    s <- rowSums(d)
    s[s <= 0] <- .Machine$double.xmin
    w  <- d[, 1] / s
    sw <- sum(w)
    if (!is.finite(sw) || sw < 1 || (length(x) - sw) < 1) return(one())
    a   <- c(sw / length(x), 1 - sw / length(x))
    tau <- c(sum(w * x) / sw, sum((1 - w) * x) / (length(x) - sw))
    if (any(!is.finite(tau)) || any(tau <= 0)) return(one())
    ll <- sum(log(s))
    if (is.finite(ll) && is.finite(ll_old) &&
        abs(ll - ll_old) < tol * abs(ll)) break
    ll_old <- ll
  }

  o <- order(tau); tau <- tau[o]; a <- a[o]
  if (tau[2] / tau[1] < min_ratio || min(a) < min_area) return(one())

  tibble::tibble(n_components = 2L, tau_fast_ms = tau[1],
                 tau_slow_ms = tau[2], area_fast = a[1],
                 mean_ms = mean(x), n_events = length(x))
}
```

# Find the files

```{r discover}
find_one <- function(folder, pattern) {
  f <- list.files(
    folder,
    pattern = "\\.(csv|parquet)$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  hit <- f[
    grepl(pattern, basename(f), ignore.case = TRUE)
  ]

  if (!length(hit)) return(NA_character_)

  if (length(hit) > 1) {
    warning(
      folder, ": ", length(hit),
      " files match '", pattern,
      "', using ", basename(hit[1])
    )
  }

  hit[1]
}

folders <- list.dirs(CFG$pheno_root, recursive = FALSE)
if (!is.null(CFG$only)) folders <- folders[basename(folders) %in% CFG$only]
if (!length(folders)) stop("No phenotype folders in ", CFG$pheno_root)

parquets <- list.files(CFG$batch_dir, pattern = "\\.parquet$", full.names = TRUE)

manifest <- purrr::map_dfr(folders, function(fd) {
  tag <- gsub(" ", "_", basename(fd))
  ddpm <- parquets[grepl(paste0("^", tag), basename(parquets))]
  if (!length(ddpm)) ddpm <- parquets[grepl(tag, basename(parquets), fixed = TRUE)]
  tibble::tibble(
    phenotype = tag,
    raw  = find_one(fd, CFG$raw_pattern),
    gan  = find_one(fd, CFG$gan_pattern),
    ddpm = if (length(ddpm)) ddpm[1] else NA_character_
  )
})

nice_kable(
  manifest |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(raw, gan, ddpm), basename)),
  caption = "Manifest: seed, GAN and DDPM file for each phenotype."
)

bad <- manifest |> dplyr::filter(is.na(raw) | is.na(ddpm))
if (nrow(bad)) {
  warning("Dropping phenotypes with no seed or no DDPM file: ",
          paste(bad$phenotype, collapse = ", "))
  manifest <- dplyr::filter(manifest, !is.na(raw), !is.na(ddpm))
}
if (!nrow(manifest)) stop("Nothing left to analyse.")
```

# Pre-flight

Every record is read and checked before any metric is computed; a record that
cannot support the analysis stops the run here.

All records are held in memory for the rest of the notebook. `CFG$only` runs a
subset of phenotypes.

```{r preflight}
recs <- purrr::map(seq_len(nrow(manifest)), function(i) {
  row <- manifest[i, ]
  out <- list(Real = read_record(row$raw), Diffusion = read_record(row$ddpm))
  if (!is.na(row$gan)) out$GAN <- read_record(row$gan)
  out
})
names(recs) <- manifest$phenotype

n_before <- purrr::imap_dfr(recs, function(arms, ph)
  tibble::tibble(phenotype = ph, arm = names(arms),
                 n_read = vapply(arms, nrow, integer(1))))

# Seed record inventory, at full length (before cropping).
seed_inventory <- purrr::imap_dfr(recs, function(arms, ph) {
  d  <- arms$Real
  fs <- fs_of(d)
  tibble::tibble(
    phenotype  = ph,
    seed_file  = basename(manifest$raw[manifest$phenotype == ph]),
    n_rows     = nrow(d),
    sample_khz = round(fs / 1000, 3),
    duration_s = nrow(d) / fs,
    max_levels = max(d$channels),
    popen      = mean(d$channels > 0),
    mean_pA    = mean(d$current),
    sd_pA      = stats::sd(d$current))
})

nice_kable(seed_inventory, digits = 4, label = "seed_inventory",
           caption = paste("Seed records as read, before any",
                           "cropping. n_rows is the number of usable rows",
                           "read from each file."))

readr::write_csv(seed_inventory, file.path(CFG$out_dir, "table1_seed_data.csv"))
```

```{r preflight-crop}
# Full-length diffusion records for the block-join test (cropping would drop
# the later joins). Used only by the seam figures.
recs_full_diffusion <- purrr::map(recs, function(arms) arms$Diffusion)

# GAN and Diffusion are cropped to the shorter of the two (in rows), since
# several metrics depend on length (MMD z, permutation p, KS, spectral
# distances) and the two arms are compared head to head. Real keeps its full
# length: it is the fixed reference, and the equivalence margins come from it.
# In practice the GAN length sets arm_min_len.
for (ph in names(recs)) {
  arms <- recs[[ph]]
  sim_names <- setdiff(names(arms), "Real")
  arm_min_len <- Inf
  for (a in sim_names) { arm_min_len <- min(arm_min_len, nrow(arms[[a]])) }
  for (a in sim_names) { arms[[a]] <- crop_rows(arms[[a]], arm_min_len) }
  recs[[ph]] <- arms
}

crop_report <- n_before |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    purrr::imap_dfr(recs, function(arms, ph)
      tibble::tibble(phenotype = ph, arm = names(arms),
                     n_used = vapply(arms, nrow, integer(1)))),
    by = c("phenotype", "arm")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(kept = n_used / n_read)

nice_kable(crop_report, digits = 3, label = "crop_report",
             caption = paste("Rows read and rows retained. Real keeps its full length;",
                              "GAN and Diffusion are cropped to the shorter of the two."))
readr::write_csv(crop_report, file.path(CFG$out_dir, "crop_report.csv"))
```

```{r preflight-inventory}
inventory <- purrr::imap_dfr(recs, function(arms, ph) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(arms, function(d, a) {
    closed <- d$current[d$channels == 0]
    open   <- d$current[d$channels > 0]
    tibble::tibble(
      phenotype = ph, arm = a, n = nrow(d),
      has_time = !grepl("time=none", attr(d, "map")),
      fs = fs_of(d),
      longest_closed = longest_at(d, "closed"),
      longest_open   = longest_at(d, "open"),
      popen = mean(d$channels > 0), max_level = max(d$channels),
      baseline = median(closed),
      unit_amp = median(open) - median(closed),
      cols = attr(d, "map"))
  })
})

# Catch arms that were min-max scaled or are in the wrong units (unitary
```
